Port drovr's agent-pane backend from herdr onto Orca, so herdr can be dropped from the user's setup.

## Why
The user is replacing their herdr-based agent/worktree flow with Orca (onorca.dev, the agent IDE; its CLI is `orca` on PATH — use that, NOT `orca-ide`, which is the GUI launcher and rejects CLI subcommands). drovr is herdr-coupled at its core: every pipeline phase and every `drovr code-review` reviewer runs in a herdr pane, via the `Herdr` trait in `cli/src/herdr.rs` (socket JSON-RPC to herdr; `FakeHerdr` for tests). That coupling is the only thing keeping herdr installed.

## What drovr has that Orca does not (keep these — they are why drovr survives)
Investigated in a dotfiles session on 2026-10-24. Usage: 200 of 244 runs under ~/.local/share/drovr/runs are `cr-*` code-review panels; 16 completed pipelines, latest `node-fencing` 2026-10-22.
1. `drovr code-review` panel: read-only multi-angle reviewers (pi on gemma), merged findings, `defer`, review-until-clean.
2. Gated pipeline with enforced `<phase>-HANDOFF.md` before `phase done`.
3. Review server: spec approval gate, `drovr ask` interview panel, push notifications.
4. Reflex hooks (SessionStart router + per-turn gate) and the discipline skills.

## What Orca already covers (candidate replacements for herdr calls)
- Worktrees: `orca worktree create --repo ... --name ... --json` (replaces `.drovr/wt/<run>`).
- Agent panes: `orca agent launch --agent claude|pi|omp --worktree <id> --prompt ... --json`, `orca worktree create --agent ...`.
- Terminal I/O: `orca terminal read|send|wait --for tui-idle|close|list --json`.
- Supervision/liveness/blocked: `orca orchestration worker-start|worker-list|check|ask|reply` (worker-list `projection.attention` ~ herdr `blocked`).
Read `orca skills get orca-cli` and `orca skills get orchestration` (plus `--reference` docs they name) before designing. `orca agent-context --json` dumps the full command schema.

## Scope / constraints
- Goal: an Orca backend behind drovr's existing pane abstraction, selectable by config (e.g. `pane_backend = "orca"`), with herdr kept working until the user says otherwise. Every drovr CLI contract in README.md (exit codes, run dir layout, `state.json` fields — `pane_id`, `tab_id`, `retired_panes`, `pane_agent`) must keep its meaning or be migrated explicitly.
- Worktree runs should become Orca-managed worktrees so they show up in Orca's sidebar.
- This is a large change: write a spec first and get the user's approval on it before writing implementation code. Use drovr's own discipline (drovr:tdd for code, drovr:code-review on every change).
- Work in this Orca worktree on its branch. Do not push to drovr's `main` or merge without the user's go-ahead.
- Out of scope: the dotfiles side (drovr `worktree = false`, main-edit guard message, autoMode cd rule). The originating dotfiles session handles that.

## Done when
The spec is approved, and a drovr build with the Orca backend selected can run a `drovr code-review run` panel and a `drovr new` pipeline end-to-end with no herdr running, with tests covering the backend through a fake like `FakeHerdr`.

#   ./tests/claude-main-edit-guard.sh
set -u

# The flake ref comes from this script's own location, not `.#`, so running it
# from a worktree tests THAT tree rather than whichever happens to be the cwd.
# The host is read from /etc/hostname because the CI job writes $TEST_HOST into
# it before running tests/ (see .forgejo/workflows/nix-eval.yml).
REPO=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)
host=$(cat /etc/hostname)

T=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$T"' EXIT
fails=0; n=0

if ! nix eval --json \
     "$REPO#homeConfigurations.$host.config.programs.claude-code.settings.hooks.PreToolUse" \
     >"$T/hooks.json" 2>"$T/err"; then
  echo "nix eval failed for $host's PreToolUse hooks:" >&2; cat "$T/err" >&2; exit 1
fi
jq -r '.[] | select(.matcher | test("Edit")) | .hooks[0].command' "$T/hooks.json" >"$T/hook.sh"
[ -s "$T/hook.sh" ] || { echo "no PreToolUse hook matches Edit" >&2; exit 1; }

# The hook calls jq and git by store path, and eval alone does not realise
# them: on a box that has never switched to this config they are not there.
for p in $(grep -o '/nix/store/[^/ ]*' "$T/hook.sh" | sort -u); do
  [ -e "$p" ] || nix build --no-link "$p" 2>"$T/err" \
    || { echo "could not realise $p:" >&2; cat "$T/err" >&2; exit 1; }
done

# Commits need an identity and a throwaway repo has none; nothing reads it.
export GIT_AUTHOR_NAME=t GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL= GIT_COMMITTER_NAME=t GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL=
export GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=/dev/null

verdict() { # verdict <file path> [VAR=value ...] -> allow | deny
  local f=$1 out; shift
  out=$(printf '{"tool_input":{"file_path":"%s"}}' "$f" | env "$@" bash "$T/hook.sh")
  case "$out" in
    "") echo allow ;;
    *'"permissionDecision":"deny"'*) echo deny ;;
    *) echo "unexpected: $out" ;;
  esac
}

check() { # check <what> <expected> <actual>
  n=$((n+1))
  if [ "$2" = "$3" ]; then
    echo "ok   $1"
  else
    echo "FAIL $1"; echo "     expected: $2"; echo "     actual:   $3"
    fails=$((fails+1))
  fi
}

# A primary checkout on master, with `topic` conflicting with it on f and
# `clean` adding a file of its own. Each scenario below gets a fresh one, so
# none inherits the state the last one left -- a second merge of an
# already-merged branch is "Already up to date" and sets nothing up at all.
mkrepo() { # mkrepo <name>; sets R
  R="$T/$1"
  git init -q -b master "$R"
  echo base > "$R/f"; git -C "$R" add f; git -C "$R" commit -q -m base
  git -C "$R" checkout -q -b topic
  echo topic > "$R/f"; git -C "$R" commit -q -am topic
  git -C "$R" checkout -q -b clean master
  echo clean > "$R/k"; git -C "$R" add k; git -C "$R" commit -q -m clean
  git -C "$R" checkout -q master
  echo master > "$R/f"; git -C "$R" commit -q -am master
}

conflicted() { # conflicted <what>: the fixture must really have left a conflict

}

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /nix/store/REDACTED/skills/code-review

# Code Review

## Overview

**They find, you fix.** Follow the spirit, not the letter: dispatching a
reviewer satisfies the letter; one that read an empty diff, or that you never
waited for, looked at nothing and found nothing. The rule is that
somebody who did not write the change has said what is wrong with it — and that
cannot be you. You read the change you meant to make, not the one on disk.

**Write for the agent who inherits this: the next phase agent is you, with your
context gone.** A finding you settled in your head is one they meet as a bug,
with nothing saying anyone saw it.

## The Iron Law

```
NO CHANGE IS DONE UNTIL A READ-ONLY REVIEWER HAS SEEN IT AND
EVERY CRITICAL AND IMPORTANT FINDING IS RESOLVED OR RECORDED AS DEFERRED.
```

**Read-only** is a trust boundary, not a performance note: the reviewer reads
anything, runs read-only checks, and writes nothing — not source, not git, not
run state. You stay the single writer.

No exceptions. The first names its addressee; the rest hold for anyone.

- **Never run a reviewer in the background — you, the agent in a herdr pane,
  where ending a turn *is* how you report done.** Do not set
  `run_in_background`, do not yield, and do not schedule a wakeup while one is
  out. A backgrounded reviewer parks you mid-turn, indistinguishable from a
  finished turn, and the run stalls until a human nudges the pane. Dispatch it
  blocking and read its verdict in the turn you dispatched it. That reason is
  role-specific, so there is exactly one role it does not bind: a **driver**
  reviewing its own inline change, which may background the panel and end the
  turn because its harness re-invokes it on process exit. Inside a pipeline
  run the driver has no panel to background — the task agent's is the gate,
  and `skills/pipeline/SKILL.md` says so at its own loop. In a pane, the
  prohibition is yours.
- **Do not judge a change too small to review.** A one-line edit to a condition
  is the size this skill exists for. Dispatch a reviewer over it.
- **Do not count your own read as the review.** Re-reading your diff tells you
  it matches what you intended — the one thing never in doubt. Dispatch someone
  who does not know it.
- **Do not leave it for the pipeline's review phase.** That phase reads what you
  hand it, after later work is built on it. Dispatch here, while the change is
  one commit wide.
- **Do not close a finding by disagreeing with it.** When you will not fix one,
  quote it and write the reason in the report or handoff. An unrecorded
  decision reads downstream like an unread finding.
- **Do not repeat a verdict you have not read.** Open the file the reviewer
  names, or re-run the review when it named none. A reviewer that never came
  back has not said "clean".

## Announce

Say this out loud before dispatching anything:

```
Using drovr:code-review — dispatching read-only reviewers before calling this done.
```

## The procedure

> When a skill or briefing gives you a numbered checklist, create **one tracked item per step**
> using whatever task tool this harness exposes — `TodoWrite`, or `TaskCreate`/`TaskUpdate` —
> before you start step 1. Mark each in-progress when you start it and complete when its
> evidence is in hand. If the harness exposes no task tool, write the checklist to
> `~/.local/share/drovr/runs/<run>/checklist.md` when inside a run, or `CHECKLIST.md` at the
> repo root otherwise, and tick items there. An untracked checklist decays with the context
> window; that decay is the exact failure drovr exists to fight.

Re-create those items for each change you review, not once for the session.

1. **Write down the change and the exact range** — the files, and `<base>..HEAD`.
   Get it wrong and the reviewer reports clean on nothing.
2. **Dispatch read-only reviewers, blocking, one per angle:** run
   `drovr code-review run <run> <task>` (`<base>` from `<task>-base.sha`, recorded
   before your first edit) — or, **inline** with no run,
   `drovr code-review run --base "$(git merge-base HEAD main)" <task>`. Nothing
   else, and never invent a run to get one.

   It spawns one reviewer per **configured** angle — `config.angles`, which
   defaults to correctness, security, error-handling, type-design — each writing
   `<task>-review-<angle>.json`, merged into `<task>-review.json`. **Read the
   config, not this page**, and cover any lens it omits yourself.

   Tell each reviewer to review as a skeptic, not the author; to say whether the
   tests exercise the behaviour, not just that they pass; to rate every finding
   **Critical, Important or nit** — what the Iron Law gates on — and say so when
   it found none; and to write them to a path you name, so step 3 has something
   to open. The lenses to cover:
   - **Spec compliance** — what was agreed, no more, no less?
   - **Correctness** — real bugs, unhandled cases, broken invariants.
   - **Verification** — do the claimed tests exist, and would they fail on a
     regression?
   - **Quality** — reuse, simplification, consistency with the code around it.
3. **Wait for every reviewer, then read what each wrote.** Open the findings
   file by path, then classify the round by how the panel exited:

   | Exit | What it means |
   |---|---|
   | 0 | clean — a real range was reviewed, nothing blocking |
   | 3 | blocking findings; go to step 5 |
   | 2 | timeout — reviewers are slow, not broken. Re-run the same command: it resumes the panel in flight |
   | 1 | error, or an empty `<base>..HEAD` it refused. Fix the range or the setup; never re-run blindly |
   | 137/143 | **your own harness killed it.** drovr produced no verdict at all, and none of the rows above describes the run. Re-run to resume, and record the round as **unclassifiable** — never as a timeout |

   A reviewer that returned no verdict is none of the five: re-dispatch rather
   than report its silence.

   **Only 0 is clean, and one clean round does not end the loop.** Stop at
   whichever of two comes first — **there is no round cap**, and a loop still
   turning up Critical or Important findings is not finished at any count:
   - **Two consecutive clean rounds over an unchanged HEAD.** Any edit between
     them resets the count — the second round is evidence about the first only
     if it read the same code.
   - **Two consecutive rounds that lost a dimension** — its own outcome, *not*
     a clean ending: a missing angle is a Critical stand-in, so a round that
     lost a reviewer never measured the code, and a panel that keeps failing to
     deliver is not going to. Name the angles that never ran, write up every
     round's verdict and everything still open (step 5), and finish on that
     record rather than on a verdict. Without this a panel whose reviewers keep
     dying cannot end at all, since such a round is never clean.

   Two caveats the rule owes you. Two cleans make a false clean **less
   likely**, not unlikely, and prove nothing about convergence — in forge#88's
   own data two consecutive cleans preceded a `changes` round with seven
   findings. And every word of this is prose nothing enforces — the
   shape of the *"re-run it"* that produced 47 re-arms over 14 hours.
4. **Check what the reviewer actually read — range *and* working tree.** The
   range must be the whole of `<base>..HEAD`, every file you touched, not a
   subset you picked; **and uncommitted work is in scope, not exempt** — drovr's
   panel reviews the diff *plus the current working tree*. A verdict covers what
   is on disk only if the reviewer saw both. Clean on an empty range, a subset,
   or a tree with unreviewed edits in it is about a change nobody read.
5. **Resolve every Critical and Important finding, or record the deferral with
   `drovr code-review defer`.** Per finding: quote it, then name the edit
   answering it by file — or, if you are not making it, run

   ```
   drovr code-review defer <RUN> <TASK> --file <path> [--line <n>] \
     --severity <critical|important|nit> --summary "<the finding>" \
     --reason "<why it is not being fixed>"
   ```

   A deferral written only in prose is one the next round cannot read, so it
   re-raises the finding you already ruled on. The command appends to a
   per-task log every later seed carries; prose does not.
6. **Re-run the checks after your last review-driven edit, then say it is
   done.** The fixes are new, unverified code: run the tests. When the change is
   not code and has no suite, name what you re-read instead and why it covers the
   edits — written down, never assumed. Report the findings, the edits and the
   deferrals; inside a drovr phase this also gates `drovr phase done`. **Done is
   step 3's termination rule met, not the first exit 0** — say which of the
   two ended it, and on a lost dimension say plainly that the loop ended on a
   record rather than on a clean verdict.

## Requirements

The middle column is what the claim takes; the right is what gets accepted
instead.

| The claim | Required evidence | NOT sufficient |
|---|---|---|
| *"This change has been reviewed"* | A read-only reviewer dispatched over this change in the foreground, returned in this turn, and the range you handed it, written down | Your own re-read · a reviewer launched and not waited for · a review of the tree before your last edit |
| *"The reviewer found nothing"* | The findings file it wrote, opened by path and read by you — or the review re-run by you when it wrote none — **and** what it read shown to be the whole of `<base>..HEAD` **plus your working tree** | Its summary, however much output it pastes · exit 1 or 2 · a subset of your files · uncommitted edits nobody looked at · a verdict that never arrived |
| *"Every Critical and Important finding is resolved"* | Each quoted, the edit answering it named by file, and step 6's checks re-run after the last edit | A count · agreeing with one in prose · fixing the Criticals and leaving the Importants |
| *"That finding does not apply here"* | The finding quoted, and the reason written where the next agent reads it | Deciding it in your head · *"out of scope"* with no scope named · silence, which downstream reads as resolved |

## Red flags — STOP

Some are thoughts, some are things you have just written. Either way you are at
the line.

- *"They are going to read it line by line anyway."* · *"The lead said just
  send it."* · *"It is a two-line change."* · *"I already reviewed it myself."*
  · *"The pipeline's review phase will catch it."* — each opens a row in
  *Rationalizations*, verbatim. Go do the thing in its row.
- *You are about to launch a reviewer in the background and keep working.* →
  Dispatch it blocking. No version of that ends with you reading its verdict
  this turn.
- *A reviewer has not come back and you are writing the report.* → Block on it.
  Silence is not a pass; a parked reviewer is not a finished one.
- *The panel came back clean in seconds on a large diff.* → Check what it read.
  Clean and empty look identical from here.
- **Anything that treats the change as finished** — any wording at all, and
  also committing, opening a PR, or starting the next task — while a reviewer is
  unread, unreturned, or holding an unresolved Critical or Important finding. If
  you cannot name the reviewer and point at what it wrote, change what you
  dispatched, not how you word it.

## Rationalizations

The right column is an instruction, not an argument. Do the thing in it.

| The thought | Do this instead |
|---|---|
| *"They are going to read it line by line anyway."* | Dispatch the reviewer first, then send it. Two different reads: theirs is for fit, the review's is for correctness, and one does not make the other redundant — reading a document aloud catches prose gaps, not retry semantics. |
| *"The lead said just send it."* | Send it after the review, and tell them the call moves. That is a scheduling reflex, not anyone weighing the technical risk — the calendar is theirs, the correctness yours. |
| *"It is a two-line change."* | Dispatch a reviewer over the two lines. Size is not a risk measure, and the risk you estimate in order to skip the review is what it would have told you. |
| *"I already reviewed it myself."* | Dispatch one that did not write it. Your read confirms the diff matches your intent; the defects worth catching are in what you did not think of. |
| *"The pipeline's review phase will catch it."* | Dispatch here, now. That phase reads what you hand it, after later tasks built on it; a finding costs more at every step it survives. |
| *"The reviewer came back with no findings."* | Open the file it named, and check it read your whole change, working tree included. An empty range comes back clean from every angle at once. |

## Worked example

One read away, in `skills/code-review/worked-example.md`: a 320-line spec, a
client call in 19 minutes, a $45,000 sign-off and a lead writing *"just send
it"* — the rationalization refused, the panel run, two Importants found, the
call moved 22 minutes. Worth reading once; the rules above do not depend on it.

## Cross-refs

- `drovr:verification-before-completion` — REQUIRED before you repeat a
  verdict: a reviewer's report is a claim, not evidence.
- `drovr:systematic-debugging` — REQUIRED when a finding is a bug: it is a
  report, not a diagnosis. Reproduce before you fix.
- `drovr:tdd` — REQUIRED when a finding needs new behaviour: the fix is new code
  and gets a failing test.
- `drovr:handoff` — REQUIRED at a phase boundary: deferred findings travel in the
  handoff or not at all.
- `drovr:pipeline` — whose gate this is in a run: yours, the task agent's, run
  to step 3's termination rule before `drovr phase done`. The driver reads your
  record of it and runs no panel of its own.

The tree is clean at HEAD e1253a5c, and `bash tests/claude-main-edit-guard.sh` passes (122 cases, 0 failed, run as shiori), but the suite can't catch this bug.

## Critical (conditional)

**`<<<"$input"` breaks the hook under dash** (home.nix:1872, 1898, 1899; added in 95c5a006).
- Claude Code runs hook commands with `/bin/sh -c` (I checked the hook spawn code in claude-code 2.1.308).
- I ran the rendered hook under dash 0.5.13: `Syntax error: redirection unexpected`, exit 2, for every input. That includes linked worktrees, files outside git, and runs with `CLAUDE_ALLOW_MAIN_EDIT` set.
- For a PreToolUse hook, exit 2 means deny. So every Edit, Write and NotebookEdit is refused on any host whose `/bin/sh` is dash.
- shiori and utsuho (Arch) are fine: `/bin/sh` is bash there. macOS `/bin/sh` is bash too, so mari is fine. It's Critical if fujiwara, chiyari or kyuusaku uses dash, and only latent otherwise. kyuusaku's `/local/mnt/workspace` home suggests a Debian/Ubuntu-style box.
- **Fix:** `printf '%s' "$input" | jq ...` (POSIX).
- **Test gap:** the suite runs the hook with `bash "$T/hook.sh"`, so it can't see this. It should also run the hook under `sh -c` and dash.

## Important

None.

## Nits

1. **Wrong root check (home.nix:1900, no-Orca text).** "unless that path is the checkout root itself" assumes drovr records the repo root. drovr actually records the directory it was launched from (`current_dir()`, or `--dir`). For a `--no-worktree` run launched from `/repo/cli`, a phase agent runs EnterWorktree on a plain subdirectory, which fails. Its next fallback is "EnterWorktree with a name", which takes it off its run. Suggested wording: "is this checkout (<r>) or a directory inside it".
2. **Circular for the driver (home.nix:1900).** A `--no-worktree` run's driver reads "stop and report … which only its driver can do" and is effectively told to report to itself. Re-running `drovr new` with the same name is refused as a duplicate.
3. **Wrong advice for `--worktree` runs on Orca hosts.** A phase agent of a run made with `drovr new --worktree` that strays into the primary checkout is told the run must be relaunched. The run is already isolated; the right move is EnterWorktree on `drovr path`. This is rare.
4. **No `cd` rule for `.drovr/wt` on Orca hosts (home.nix:2087).** `--worktree` still creates `.drovr/wt` there, so a driver that `cd`s into one gets no rule. Low impact: drovr itself says to use EnterWorktree, not `cd`.
5. **Test cleanups (tests/claude-main-edit-guard.sh):**
   - Line 29: neither `/etc/hostname` nor `/proc` exists on darwin, so on mari the suite dies with an empty host name. `uname -n` works on both.
   - Line 145: a dead `reason=` assignment.
   - Line 137: a redundant `env` in `refusal "$R/f" env CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=/proj`.
   - home.nix:2764: "the reason `worktree = true` existed" reads as if the key were gone, but it is still `true` on four hosts.

## Each role's deny reason
- **Inline agent:** correct on all six hosts. The four no-Orca hosts render the same text, as do shiori and utsuho.
- **drovr driver:** correct, apart from nit 2.
- **drovr phase agent:** correct, apart from nits 1 and 3.
- **Against drovr's source and README:** the `worktree` key defaults to true, `--no-worktree` beats `--worktree` beats config, and `drovr path` prints the worktree or the launch dir. All match.
- **orca:** the `orca worktree create` flags exist. `orca` itself is only on PATH inside Orca terminals (via a shim), so the hook's "may not be on PATH" comment and its "if that command fails" fallback are both right.

Other checks passed:
- **Nix escaping:** `''${…}` renders as `${…}`, and the nested `''` strings render cleanly with no `'` inside the jq program.
- **Syntax and stdin:** `bash -n` passes on both variants, and stdin is read once.
- **`hasOrca`:** it matches orca.nix's install gate.

## Critical
None.

## Important
**I1. On Orca hosts, a phase agent in a run that is already isolated is told to stop the run** (`home.nix:1900`, Orca text)
- **Scenario:** the run was launched correctly from `~/orca/workspaces/dotfiles/<task>`, or with `drovr new --worktree`. A phase agent there edits the primary checkout by absolute path. That is plausible in this repo, because the auto-mode text names "the dotfiles repo at ~/devel/dotfiles".
- **What it's told:** "drovr phase agent, do not move: stop and report that the run must be relaunched from an Orca worktree".
- **What happens:** following that halts a healthy run. The driver then relaunches from an Orca worktree the run is already in. The right action is to edit the same file inside its own worktree.
- **On hosts without Orca:** the same agent is told to EnterWorktree on `drovr path <run>`, which is the directory it is already in. The retry is refused again, so it loops instead of halting.
- **Overlap:** this is close to the decided item "an agent already in a worktree told to make another", but the result here is a stopped run. Drop it if you count it as covered.
- **Fix:** add one clause: "if your working directory is already a linked worktree, edit this file's counterpart there."

## Nits
1. **The `--no-worktree` test compares exact strings** (`home.nix:1900`, no-Orca text). `drovr path` prints the launch directory or `--dir` argument as typed, without canonicalizing it (drovr `main.rs:1420-1438`, `cmd_path` at `:1592`).
   - A run launched from `repo/sub` or with `--dir .` doesn't match "the checkout root itself (/repo)".
   - The agent then calls EnterWorktree on a path git doesn't list as a worktree, which is rejected. That branch has no "if that fails" step.
   - Fix: say "inside this checkout" instead of "is the checkout root itself".
2. **A `--worktree` run's driver on an Orca host is sent to Orca, not to its run** (`home.nix:2774-2776` vs `:1900`). The drovr comment says `--worktree` still works where the key is false. But the Orca refusal has no `drovr path` sentence, so a driver that never entered its `.drovr/wt` worktree makes an Orca worktree, and its edits land on a branch the run doesn't own.
3. **The comment "Either way the fallback is EnterWorktree's own .claude/worktrees" is inaccurate** (`home.nix:1890`). In the no-Orca text, that step only covers agents that are not in a drovr run. The test's own comment at `:188-189` says so.
4. **The `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` comment's reasoning is wrong after EnterWorktree** (`home.nix:1894-1897`). I checked this in the claude-code 2.1.308 binary:
   - The hook environment sets `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` to the launch-time project root.
   - EnterWorktree moves the transcript into the worktree's project folder but does not update that root.
   - So after entering a worktree, `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` is where the session was launched, not where it is stored.
   - `--resume` has explicit handling for sessions recorded in a worktree, so the suggested command very likely still works. I didn't run it because it would start a session.
   - The `.cwd` fallback is effectively never reached for local hooks.
5. **"A run edits the checkout it was launched from" ignores `--dir`** (`home.nix:2759`).
6. **Several sentences in the refusal are not pinned by the test** (`tests/claude-main-edit-guard.sh:175-196`). Each change below would still pass all 122 cases:
   1. Swapping or ungating the Orca phase-agent clause: "do not move" and "Otherwise" are unchecked.
   2. Changing what the agent does after each command: "EnterWorktree on the worktree path in its JSON output", "If that command fails", and "EnterWorktree on the path" (no-Orca) are unchecked.
   3. Dropping "which only its driver can do".
   4. Dropping "You cannot set it yourself" or "must not route around this guard through Bash".
   5. Negating a clause, e.g. "do NOT run `drovr path <run>`", since every check is a substring match.

## How each role is handled
- **Orca hosts:**
  - Inline and non-drovr agents: correct. The `orca worktree create` flags match its `--help`.
  - A run launched from the primary checkout, or `--no-worktree`: the phase agent is told to stop and report, which is correct. Its driver is moved, not the run (decided item).
  - A phase agent in a run that is already isolated: wrong (I1).
- **Hosts without Orca:**
  - Inline and non-drovr agents: correct.
  - A driver that never entered its worktree: correct. EnterWorktree accepts `.drovr/wt/<run>`.
  - A `--no-worktree` agent: correct only when the printed path is exactly the repo root (nit 1).

- **The override sentence:** correct on every host.

# --- the guard itself --------------------------------------------------------
check "primary checkout on master: edit refused" deny "$(verdict "$R/f")"
check "a file that does not exist yet is refused too" deny "$(verdict "$R/new/dir/g")"
check "CLAUDE_ALLOW_MAIN_EDIT=1 lets it through" allow \
  "$(verdict "$R/f" CLAUDE_ALLOW_MAIN_EDIT=1)"
# The refusal names the way out. Where Orca is installed (orca.nix: GUI Linux)
# that is an Orca worktree of this repo; elsewhere drovr keeps its own
# .drovr/wt worktrees, so it is EnterWorktree, and `drovr path` for a run.
# Neither suggests a bare in-repo `git worktree add`: its untracked dir makes
# hms refuse the primary checkout.
orca_on() { # orca_on <host> -> true | false; exits non-zero on an eval failure,
           # which each call site turns into the suite failing
  local v
  v=$(nix eval --raw "$REPO#homeConfigurations.$1.config.home.packages" \
    --apply 'ps: if builtins.any (p: (p.pname or "") == "orca") ps then "true" else "false"') \
    || { echo "could not evaluate $1's packages" >&2; exit 1; }
  case "$v" in true|false) echo "$v" ;; *) echo "orca_on $1: got '$v'" >&2; exit 1 ;; esac
}
refusal() { # refusal <file path> [VAR=value ...] -> deny reason, session sid-1 in /cwd
  printf '{"session_id":"sid-1","cwd":"/cwd","tool_input":{"file_path":"%s"}}' "$1" \
    | env -u CLAUDE_ALLOW_MAIN_EDIT -u CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR "${@:2}" bash "$T/hook.sh" \
    | jq -r '.hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecisionReason'
}
says() { case "$reason" in *"$1"*) echo yes ;; *) echo no ;; esac; }
here=$(orca_on "$host") || exit 1
reason=$(refusal "$R/f")
if [ "$here" = true ]; then
  check "refusal names an Orca worktree of this repo" yes "$(says "orca worktree create --repo path:$R ")"
  # The repo root, not the directory the hook walked up to from a new file.
  reason=$(refusal "$R/new/dir/g")
  check "refusal for a new nested file still names the repo root" yes "$(says "--repo path:$R ")"
else
  check "refusal names no orca command on a host without it" no "$(says 'orca worktree create')"
  check "refusal points a drovr run at its own worktree" yes "$(says 'drovr path <run>')"
fi
check "refusal falls back to EnterWorktree's own worktree" yes "$(says 'EnterWorktree with a name')"
# --resume with this session's id, from its own directory: --continue picks the
# most recent conversation there, which need not be the refused one.
check "refusal names the override for exactly this session" yes \
  "$(says '`cd /cwd && CLAUDE_ALLOW_MAIN_EDIT=1 claude --resume sid-1`')"
# The session is stored under its project dir, not wherever a `cd` left it.
reason=$(refusal "$R/f" env CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=/proj)
check "the override resumes from the project dir when Claude names one" yes \
  "$(says '`cd /proj && CLAUDE_ALLOW_MAIN_EDIT=1 claude --resume sid-1`')"

  | jq -r '.hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecisionReason')
check "with no session in the input the override still reads as a command" yes \
  "$(says '`cd <this directory> && CLAUDE_ALLOW_MAIN_EDIT=1 claude --resume <session id>`')"
reason=$(refusal "$R/f")

# Every host in the flake, not just this one: the hook text, drovr's own
# worktrees and the auto-mode cd rules all follow whether Orca is installed.
hosts=$(nix eval --json "$REPO#homeConfigurations" --apply builtins.attrNames) \
  || { echo "could not list homeConfigurations" >&2; exit 1; }
hosts=$(jq -r '.[]' <<<"$hosts")
with=0; without=0
for h in $hosts; do
  orca=$(orca_on "$h") || exit 1
  if [ "$orca" = true ]; then with=$((with+1)); wt=false; else without=$((without+1)); wt=true; fi
  toml=$(nix eval --raw "$REPO#homeConfigurations.$h.config.xdg.configFile.\"drovr/config.toml\".text") \

    || { echo "could not evaluate $h's hooks" >&2; exit 1; }
  hook=$(jq -r '[.[] | select(.matcher | test("Edit")) | .hooks[0].command] | first // ""' <<<"$hook")
  # Run this host's own refusal program, not just grep it: CI runs the live hook
  # only as an Orca host, so a broken no-Orca branch would otherwise pass here
  # and, as invalid jq, emit nothing -- which lets every edit through.
  # The jq program between its quotes. Tied to the hook's exact spelling of
  # `--arg c "$cwd" '...'`: a respelling fails every host loudly, not silently.
  prog=${hook#*--arg c \"\$cwd\" \'}; prog=${prog%%\'*}

  check "$h: refusal sends a drovr run to drovr path iff drovr makes worktrees" "$wt" \

  check "$h: refusal falls back to EnterWorktree's own worktree" yes "$(says 'EnterWorktree with a name')"
  check "$h: refusal names the override for exactly this session" yes \
    "$(says '`cd /cwd && CLAUDE_ALLOW_MAIN_EDIT=1 claude --resume sid-1`')"
  check "$h: refusal keeps the override from drovr phase agents" yes "$(says 'not for a drovr phase agent')"
  check "$h: refusal suggests no in-repo git worktree" no "$(says 'git worktree add')"
  check "$h: refusal never says to relaunch with drovr new" no "$(says 'drovr new')"
  # A drovr phase agent cannot relaunch its own run: it is told to stop and
  # report, and what the run needs follows from how drovr isolates it here.
  check "$h: refusal tells a drovr phase agent to stop and report" yes "$(says 'stop and report')"
  check "$h: refusal relaunches a run from an Orca worktree iff Orca" "$orca" \
    "$([ "$(says 'relaunched from an Orca worktree')" = yes ] && echo true || echo false)"
  # drovr's own worktrees are inside the checkout (.drovr/wt), so only the root
  # itself marks a --no-worktree run; and the generic fallback is for agents
  # outside a run, not the else of that test.
  check "$h: a --no-worktree run is the checkout root itself iff drovr isolates" "$wt" \
    "$([ "$(says 'is the checkout root itself (/x)')" = yes ] && echo true || echo false)"
  check "$h: the generic fallback is for agents outside a drovr run" "$wt" \
    "$([ "$(says 'If you are not in a drovr run, EnterWorktree with a name')" = yes ] && echo true || echo false)"
  check "$h: refusal relaunches a run without --no-worktree iff drovr isolates" "$wt" \
    "$([ "$(says 'relaunched without --no-worktree')" = yes ] && echo true || echo false)"
  allow=$(nix eval --json "$REPO#homeConfigurations.$h.config.programs.claude-code.settings.autoMode.allow") \
    || { echo "could not evaluate $h's auto-mode rules" >&2; exit 1; }
  check "$h: auto mode allows cd into .drovr/wt iff drovr makes them" "$wt" \
    "$(jq -r 'any(.[]; test("into a drovr worktree"))' <<<"$allow")"
  check "$h: auto mode allows cd into an Orca worktree" true \
    "$(jq -r 'any(.[]; test("into an Orca worktree"))' <<<"$allow")"

check "hosts with Orca and without both exist" "yes yes" \

git -C "$R" worktree add -q "$T/wt" topic
